title: A new PrismaClient in each route or function opens its own connection pool and runs the database out of connections under real traffic
symptoms: Requests fail with too many connections or connection pool timeout errors once more than a handful of people use the app
The database dashboard shows far more open connections than active users
cause: In a serverless deployment each function instance makes its own PrismaClient, and each client keeps its own connection pool. A client created inside a route, or in every route file, multiplies those pools, and concurrent functions during a traffic spike can use up the database's connection limit quickly.
fix: Create one PrismaClient in a shared module, outside any handler, and import it everywhere. Keep each function's pool small, and put a connection pooler (such as PgBouncer, or your host's pooled connection string) between the functions and the database.
affected: Apps that use Prisma Client from serverless functions, Next.js Route Handlers, Server Actions or API Routes
